record.title: Idle GUI burst close runs another sandbox's untimed docker execs inline on unrelated tool threads and human approval/audit threads
record.description: close_idle_gui_bursts() iterates every sandbox's open GUI burst and is called before the per-sandbox tool_concurrency check at the start of every call_tool (service.py:273), from expire_stale (service.py:373, reached by GET /approvals, GET /approvals/{aid}, and POST /approvals/{aid} via decide->expire_stale at 385), and from GET /audit (api.py:258). Closing sandbox B's burst runs desktop_processes (ps + an xdotool search via _x) and workspace_manifest (find) and kill_processes against B's container with docker exec_run and no deadline. So B's maintenance runs on sandbox A's tool_pool thread or on a human request (Starlette threadpool) thread, outside B's tool_concurrency budget. If B's container/X server is unresponsive, the exec never returns and the unrelated caller blocks indefinitely. The burst is popped before closing (service.py:232), so one idle stuck burst permanently steals one caller thread; aggregating across many desktop sandboxes can exhaust the shared pools. The parent reproduced the cross-sandbox block against the real Docker-backed control plane: with B's Xvfb stopped and B's burst idle, A's list_dir did not return within 20s and returned 0.3s after B's Xvfb resumed.
record.root_cause: close_idle_gui_bursts() runs cross-sandbox maintenance (burst close) inline on whatever thread calls it - a tool_pool thread of an unrelated sandbox (service.py:273, before the tool_concurrency check at 275-278) or a human request thread (expire_stale service.py:373 from GET/POST approvals and decide; GET /audit api.py:258) - and the docker execs it performs (desktop_processes xdotool via _x sandbox.py:684/690-691, workspace_manifest find 499, kill_processes 697) use exec_run with no deadline, unlike exec/read_file/outbox_read which wrap the command in 'timeout'. An unresponsive owning container therefore blocks the unrelated caller indefinitely, with the work charged to no sandbox's budget.
record.intended_behavior: Work done for sandbox B should be charged to B's tool_concurrency budget and never run inline on another sandbox's tool thread or a human request thread, and every docker exec (as exec/read_file/outbox_read already do) should carry a deadline so an unresponsive container cannot stall unrelated sandboxes or the human approval/audit path.

trace.description: Agent of sandbox A posts any tool; it runs on the shared 32-thread tool_pool via run_in_executor (api.py:81,209-210). The same close_idle_gui_bursts maintenance is also reached from GET /audit (api.py:258) and, via expire_stale, from GET /approvals (217), GET /approvals/{aid} (222) and POST /approvals/{aid} decide (240-252) - all def routes on the Starlette threadpool.
close_idle_gui_bursts() runs before the per-sandbox _busy/tool_concurrency check at 275-278, so the burst-close work is charged to no sandbox's budget.

Iterates list(self._gui_burst) - every sandbox's open burst - and closes any whose last GUI input is older than gui_snapshot_idle (default 60s) on the calling thread (loop 254-256), so sandbox B is closed on sandbox A's or a human's thread.
Pops burst B (232) then calls _stop_gui_strays(B) (235) before workspace_manifest (237).
Calls self.sandboxes.desktop_processes(B) (218) against sandbox B's container.

docker exec_run of the xdotool search command (via _x at sandbox.py:684, user=desktop) with no 'timeout' wrapper, run against sandbox B's container. The calling thread (sandbox A's tool_pool thread or a human request thread) blocks in exec_start until B's X server replies; a stopped/unresponsive Xvfb never replies and exec_run has no deadline. workspace_manifest find (499) and kill_processes (697) on the same path are likewise untimed.

evidence.description: close_idle_gui_bursts() is invoked before the tool_concurrency check at 275-278, so burst-close work is never counted against any sandbox's per-sandbox budget.
The loop closes the burst of any sid in self._gui_burst, not just the calling sandbox's (254-256); _close_gui_burst pops the burst at 232 so each stuck burst costs one caller rather than all callers.
_x issues c.exec_run(argv, user=DESKTOP_USER, ...) with no 'timeout' wrapper; the docker SDK exec_run/exec_start exposes no deadline. Used by desktop_processes xdotool (690-691).

Contrast: exec wraps the command in 'timeout -k 5 <exec_timeout>' (default 60); read_file (561) and outbox_read (665) use 'timeout -k 2 30'. The burst-close execs (499 find, 684/690-691 xdotool, 697 kill) have no such bound.

expire_stale() calls close_idle_gui_bursts(); decide() calls expire_stale() first (385), so a human approve/deny decision for any approval runs another sandbox's burst-close inline on the request thread.
GET /audit calls box.close_idle_gui_bursts() on the human request (Starlette threadpool) thread before listing.

Parent Docker-backed run (l2_cross.py): with sandbox B's Xvfb stopped and B's GUI burst idle, sandbox A's list_dir did NOT return within 20s, and returned 0.3s after B's Xvfb got SIGCONT - demonstrating A's unrelated tool call blocked indefinitely on B's untimed GUI exec.

conditions.description: Lowest-trust network principal: a prompt-injected agent holding an agt_ token for a desktop-template sandbox. GUI tools have no approval gate by design (architecture: Agent -> GUI approval gate = none).
Desktop mode (Xvfb/Xfce) enabled for at least one sandbox so GUI bursts exist. Defaults: gui_snapshot_idle=60s, tool_concurrency=4, tool_pool max_workers=32 (api.py:81).

The owning container's X server (or the docker exec) must be unresponsive so the untimed exec_run does not return; docker exec_run/exec_start provides no deadline parameter. The parent induced this by SIGSTOP of Xvfb as the desktop user.
The victim's GUI burst must be idle (> gui_snapshot_idle) at the moment another sandbox's call_tool, a GET /audit, or an approval decision triggers close_idle_gui_bursts.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent on its own desktop sandbox B. Victims are other sandboxes' agents and the human operator (approval decisions and audit reads), who share the same control plane thread pools.
payloads: POST /sandboxes/{B}/tools/click  {"x":5,"y":5}   (opens a GUI burst for sandbox B)
inside B, as the desktop user (reachable via the ungated GUI tools / desktop shell): kill -STOP $(pgrep -x Xvfb)   (renders B's X server unresponsive)
stop issuing GUI input for > gui_snapshot_idle seconds so B's burst becomes idle
instructions: Create or use a desktop-template sandbox B and issue one GUI input tool so a GUI burst opens for B (service.py:_open_gui_burst via _snapshot).
From within B, make B's X server unresponsive (e.g. SIGSTOP Xvfb as the desktop user, or hold an XGrabServer); let GUI input go quiet so B's burst is idle past gui_snapshot_idle.

From an unrelated principal, trigger close_idle_gui_bursts: another sandbox A's POST /sandboxes/{A}/tools/list_dir (service.py:273), or a human GET /audit (api.py:258), or a human POST /approvals/{aid} decide (service.py:385->373).
Observe that the triggering request blocks until B's container becomes responsive again, while B's _busy/tool_concurrency counter stays unchanged.
execution.observed_result: Decisive reproduction is the parent's (l2_cross.py/.out, real Docker-backed control plane + agentbox-desktop image; I could not run Docker in the sandbox). With B's Xvfb stopped and B's burst idle, sandbox A's list_dir did not return within 20s and returned only 0.3s after B's Xvfb was resumed, confirming A's unrelated tool call blocked on B's untimed GUI exec run on A's tool_pool thread. The h-pool stub run (agents/h-pool/artifacts/h.out) independently showed that B's close runs on A's thread and on the human (expire_stale) thread while B's _busy counter stays 0, confirming the work is charged to no sandbox. Because decide() and GET /audit enter the identical close_idle_gui_bursts path on the Starlette threadpool, a human approval decision or audit read blocks the same way and the blocked thread is leaked for the burst's lifetime (burst popped at service.py:232).

remediation.strategy: Put a hard deadline on every docker exec reached from the burst-close and GUI paths (wrap the container command in 'timeout -k' as exec/read_file/outbox_read do, and/or use a client call with a socket timeout), and stop running cross-sandbox maintenance inline on an unrelated caller's thread: close idle bursts in a dedicated background worker, or charge each close to the owning sandbox's tool_concurrency budget and never to another sandbox's tool thread or a human request thread. Guard close_idle_gui_bursts/_close_gui_burst so one unresponsive container is skipped-and-logged after a bounded wait instead of stalling the loop for other sandboxes.

likelihood.reason: Requires a desktop sandbox and the agent to render its own X server/exec unresponsive; the GUI boundary is ungated by design and prompt injection is in the threat model, but weaponizing X unresponsiveness from the lowest-trust principal carries a desktop-image dependency (terminal/launcher reachability, X auth) that the parent demonstrated via a desktop-user action rather than a confirmed uid-1000-only path. The defect also triggers on benign causes (a slow or overloaded desktop container, a slow Docker exec), so exposure is not solely attacker-gated.

impact.reason: A single unresponsive desktop container indefinitely blocks an unrelated sandbox's tool call (demonstrated: 20s, bounded only by the test's external SIGCONT) and, by the identical close_idle_gui_bursts path, a human approval decision (POST /approvals/{aid}) or GET /audit, degrading the human-oversight safety function; the blocked shared control-plane thread (tool_pool of 32 or the Starlette threadpool) is leaked for the burst's lifetime. Single-principal effect is one leaked thread plus one indefinitely blocked cross-tenant request per compromised desktop sandbox (burst popped before close); aggregated across many desktop sandboxes it can exhaust both pools. Cross-tenant, persistent, poor recovery (operator must intervene).

confidence.reason: The entire source path was verified by reading: service.py:273 (before busy check 275-278), 254-256 (iterates all sandboxes), 232/235, 218 -> sandbox.py:684/690-691 untimed _x exec, with the timeout contrast at 531/561/665 and human entrypoints at api.py:258 and decide->expire_stale (385->373). The decisive runtime behaviour - the untimed exec blocks the caller indefinitely and blocks an unrelated sandbox - was reproduced by the parent against the real Docker-backed control plane and desktop image (agents/parent-live/artifacts/l2_cross.py/.out); I re-read that script and confirmed it exercises exactly this path, and I could not run it myself because the verification sandbox has no Docker. Source contains no deadline or per-sandbox accounting bound that refutes the trace.
